title: LINQ to Objects versus later SQL
hook: Bulk CSV import is LINQ to Objects: the rows are already in a List. Later SQL is a different provider with a smaller language. Do not write one query and expect both to mean the same.

sections.heading: What LINQ to Objects is
sections.prose: LINQ to Objects is Enumerable’s implementation over any IEnumerable<T> already in the process: arrays, List, Dictionary, the result of File.ReadLines, a parsed CSV. Lambdas may call any C# you could call in a foreach. Deferred execution still applies. This is the right default for import pipelines, in-memory reporting after you already loaded attempts, and Redis payloads you deserialized. It is not slower than foreach by some law; allocations from delegates, closures, and intermediate iterators are the real cost, measurable on the submit hot path.

snippets.label: CSV import with LINQ to Objects
snippets.code:
public static IReadOnlyList<AttemptRow> ParseAttempts(IEnumerable<string> lines) =>
    lines
        .Skip(1)
        .Select(line => line.Split(','))
        .Where(cols => cols.Length >= 3 && cols[0] is not "")
        .Select(cols => new AttemptRow(cols[0], cols[1], int.Parse(cols[2])))
        .ToList();

public sealed record AttemptRow(string AttemptId, string Status, int Score);
snippets.explanation: Skip/Select/Where run in process. ToList materializes before the file enumerator is lost. Pattern cols[0] is not "" is ordinary C# in a Func.

sections.heading: What changes if a SQL provider shows up later
sections.prose: A future IQueryable source will reject or mis-translate: DateTime.Now in a filter (often evaluated locally by accident), string.Format, your extension properties from C# 14, collection expressions, and switch expressions. The interview-level move is to keep translatable predicates boring (property, constant, a few string methods) and to pull to objects with ToList before you use the rest of C#. This module will not walk EF Core translations. Your answer is: LINQ to Objects is the full language; a SQL provider is a subset plus a server. Mixing them without a wall is how import code “worked on a list” and then timed out on a table.

snippets.label: Keep the wall explicit
snippets.explanation: OrdinalIgnoreCase is trivial in memory and historically awkward for some SQL providers. Doing it after ParseAttempts.ToList is honest.

interviewTakeaways: LINQ to Objects = Enumerable + in-memory sequences + full C# in lambdas.
CSV, Redis JSON, and already-loaded attempts belong here.
A later SQL provider is a different contract, not a faster List.
Materialize, then use rich C#, when translation is not guaranteed.
commonPitfalls: Copy-pasting an in-memory query onto IQueryable and shipping it.
Leaving a query over File.ReadLines un-materialized after the stream closes.
Micro-optimizing LINQ versus foreach before measuring allocations on the submit path.
